original_question: Let S be a numerical semigroup and let H(S) = N \ S be its set of gaps. Determine the genus g(S) = |H(S)| from a minimal system of generators of S when the embedding dimension e(S) is at least 3.
target_in_paper: Section 1's unnumbered formulation of the classical genus problem for numerical semigroups: given generators of a numerical semigroup, find the number of gaps (the genus); the paper notes that the embedding-dimension-2 case was solved by Sylvester and that the case e(S) >= 3 remains open. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the main object (a numerical semigroup S), the invariant to be computed (the genus g(S)=|H(S)|), the use of generators as the input data, and the restriction to embedding dimension at least 3, which is exactly the open range singled out in Section 1. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: The paper phrases the task as finding a formula in terms of the generators, not merely determining the genus by an unspecified method.
To make the question fully stand-alone, S should be presented as S=<n1,...,ne> where 0<n1<...<ne are the unique minimal generators and gcd(n1,...,ne)=1.
The paper's ambient convention is N={0,1,2,...}; accordingly H(S)=N\S.
The universal quantifier should be explicit: the problem asks for such a formula for every numerical semigroup with embedding dimension e>=3.
The paper states an equivalent representability formulation: count the positive integers that cannot be written as lambda1*n1+...+lambdae*ne with lambdai in N.
It is helpful to state explicitly that the e=2 case is excluded because Sylvester solved it; the open problem starts at e>=3.
No ambient ring or field, homogeneity, degree restriction, or nilpotency condition is involved here; adding any such hypothesis would move away from the paper's actual scope.
refined_question: Given a numerical semigroup S=<n1,...,ne> subseteq N minimally generated by positive integers 0<n1<...<ne with gcd(n1,...,ne)=1 and e>=3, find a formula, in terms of the generators n1,...,ne, for the genus g(S)=|N\S|.
equivalent_formulation: Given positive integers 0<n1<...<ne with gcd(n1,...,ne)=1 and e>=3, determine the number of positive integers that are not representable in the form lambda1*n1+...+lambdae*ne with lambda1,...,lambdae in N. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
justification: In Section 1 the paper first defines numerical semigroups, their unique minimal systems of generators, and the embedding dimension. It then says that Frobenius's second problem is to determine the cardinality of the gap set, called the genus, and immediately notes that Sylvester solved the embedding-dimension-2 case whereas the case e>=3 remains open. The relevant target is therefore the unnumbered Section 1 problem statement itself, so the faithful rewrite should ask for a formula in terms of the generators and should not broaden to algorithms, asymptotics, or special families. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
